name: Iteration
definition: At GitLab, we iterate to do the smallest valuable thing to get fast feedback and efficiently reach a desired end goal. Feedback can be from internal users (dogfooding), or through feedback from our broader user community. We validate each iteration and adjust, but not at the expense of the user experience that we deliver to our customers.

rows.under: Builds the whole thing, and the first feedback arrives at the end.
rows.justRight: Finds the smallest valuable version that a real user can react to, and ships that.
rows.over: Breaks it so small that no single piece is usable, and users see churn instead of progress.

rows.situation: When the small version is out
rows.under: Moves to the next thing without reading what happened.
rows.justRight: Validates the iteration, adjusts, and says what you now know that you did not before.
rows.over: Reverses direction on every data point, and the product never accumulates.

rows.under: Adds to it until it is the large change you were avoiding.
rows.justRight: Holds the boundary, and writes the rest down as the next iteration.
rows.over: Cuts scope so hard that what ships is below the quality users should ever see.

rows.situation: When nobody is sure the iteration worked
rows.under: Assumes it worked, because it shipped.
rows.justRight: Gets feedback from a real user or from dogfooding, and treats that as the evidence.
rows.over: Waits for statistical certainty on a change that could simply be tried.

rows.situation: When iterating would degrade the experience
rows.under: Ships the rough version anyway, because iteration is the value.
rows.justRight: Iterates without making the experience worse. Small is not a license to ship something broken.
rows.over: Refuses to ship anything short of complete, and iteration stops meaning anything.

rows.situation: When the work genuinely cannot be split
rows.under: Splits it artificially, and ships pieces that do not work on their own.
rows.justRight: Says plainly that this one is not divisible, and puts checkpoints in for feedback instead.
rows.over: Calls every large project indivisible, and nothing is ever iterated.
